messages:
pagerduty-bot: P0 - Private cluster GPU pool saturation (customer: acme-corp). Autoscaler attempted scale but stuck. Queues growing >6000 reqs. Paging infra-oncall.

samantha: acked, oncall here. seeing the paged alert. what's the scope? customer-facing impact?

raj: ACME private cluster only (eu-west-2). Metrics: gpu-pool-util 99.8%, request-queue-length increased from 200 -> 6200 over 12m. 95th latency for private endpoint up to 18s, errors ~12% on inference timeout. Hosted API unaffected.

liam: digging into cluster: autoscaler logs show repeated failed scale attempts: "Reached max node count" and a few "ImagePullBackOff" events for gpu-init daemonset on new nodes.

julia: confirmed. customer config has a hard maxNodes=12 for the gpu-pool (in their cluster config). current nodes=12. autoscaler is obeying the limit. also saw a quota error from provider 2h ago but that resolved earlier.

samantha: ok, two possible blockers: 1) customer maxNodes cap 2) image pull/ami mismatch preventing new nodes from joining. Which is the dominant failure?

raj: logs from autoscaler:

```
2026-03-15T01:12:02Z autoscaler: scale attempt recommended=16 -> attempt failed: maxNodesReached
2026-03-15T01:12:03Z autoscaler: nextAttempt in 20s
2026-03-15T01:13:10Z kubelet: failed to pull custom-gpu-init: ErrImagePull
```

liam: looks like autoscaler wants to scale to 16, but both failures occur intermittently: if we bypass the max, new nodes still sometimes fail due to image pull. So mitigation needs both tracks.

infra-oncall: @samantha i'm taking node provisioning and provider-side checks. @liam can you validate AMI/registry access? I'll check cloud quotas and any provider-side rate limits.

liam: on it. quick check: customer uses a private AMI baked last month. The AMI referenced in cluster template was deprecated — some regions have it missing -> nodes fail to boot with status "ImageNotFound". That's why image pull/launch fails.

samantha: customer contact? we should inform them about temporary traffic shaping and request limit until we restore capacity.

product-ops: pinged account team and sent an outgoing note to acme-corp support channel: "We're investigating increased latency on your private cluster, taking mitigations. Will update in 15m." (they asked for ETA)

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook suggestion: 
1) Temporarily increase cluster gpu-pool maxNodes to 20 (if quota allows).
2) Manually provision a fallback node with a compatible public AMI.
3) Reroute low-priority inference traffic to Hosted API via routing policy TTL=1.
4) If AMI needs rebuild, trigger customer's AMI bake and coordinate.

samantha: agree with runbook. For (1) we need customer permission to change their config. product-ops is on it. For (2) we can do a one-off node using our standard public GPU AMI; but need to be careful about data isolation — must ensure no customer data is on that host.

raj: If we add hosted fallback be explicit: only low-priority batch jobs go to hosted. Live low-latency requests should stay private if possible. We'll apply a weight of 0.25 to hosted fallback for the next 30m.

infra-oncall: quota check: provider account has spare GPU quota in eu-west-2, can go to 24 nodes. I'll bump nodepool.max to 20 temporarily. executing now.

infra-oncall: (edited) Node pool max increased to 20 in customer config via control-plane change. autoscaler attempted scale -> still seeing 2/4 new nodes stuck in ImagePullBackOff. I launched a manual instance with our fallback public AMI as one-off into the cluster (registered as node-aux-01).

liam: good. node-aux-01 joined successfully. kubelet shows gpus online. AVAIL capacity increased ~8%. queue length dropped from 6200 -> 4200 in 5m.

samantha: routing change to offload low-priority traffic now. rollout command:

```
POST /v1/routes/update
{ "route": "acme-private", "fallback": "redwood-hosted-gpu", "weight": 0.25, "priority":"low" }
```

raj: applied. metrics show low-priority Q length dropping, e2e latency for high-priority steady, overall errors trending down from 12% -> 6%.

julia: customer ops responded: they can temporarily lift their hard cap to 20 but will need engineering to rebuild the AMI within 24 hours. They've given approval for the temporary change.

samantha: timeline and impact
- T0 (thread_ts): paging
- T+12m: increased maxNodes -> +manual nodes
- T+18m: fallback node joined
- T+25m: routing offload applied
Current customer impact: latency reduced to 5-8s 95th, errors ~3-4%. Some background batch jobs still backlog but are being processed.

product-ops: customer asked for postmortem and for us to avoid using non-customer AMIs beyond 6 hours. Logged on account: ticket #ACME-4893.

infra-oncall: next steps for on-call: 
- monitor autoscaler attempts and image failures for 60m
- coordinate with acme engineering to confirm AMI bake; if they can't, we can offer to bake using their base image and hand over.
- create remediation PR to validate AMI existence at deploy time.

liam: quick diagnostics commands i ran:
```
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl describe pod gpu-init -n gpu-system
aws ec2 describe-images --image-ids ami-0abcd1234
```
Attach logs: `kubelet.log` showing image_not_found on 2026-03-15T01:11:58Z

samantha: I'm going to hand this over to night-oncall at 03:00 UTC. infra-oncall please maintain monitoring until handoff. @product-ops please keep customer updated every 30m until AMI is rebuilt.

infra-oncall: acknowledged. I'll leave a note in the incident channel with a short checklist and will escalate immediately if queue growth >5k again.

sre-runbook-bot: Suggested post-incident tasks (automated):
- Add pre-deploy validation step for private AMIs
- Add autoscaler alert for "maxNodes reached" paired with queue growth
- Add runbook snippet for safe hosted fallback routing

samantha: agreed. Please open follow-up tickets. I'll draft a short postmortem once we close the paging window.

product-ops: ACME-4893 updated: agreed to 24h AMI rebuild window, acceptance of temporary capacity change, wants daily updates until resolved.

night-oncall (incoming): I'm taking the handoff at 03:00 UTC. I have the control-plane session, and will watch the autoscaler logs and queue metrics. Please leave any outstanding auth tokens in 1Password and ping me if we need manual node launches.

samantha: handing off. Thanks all. :thumbsup: :eyes:

pagerduty-bot: Incident status update: mitigated -> customer-facing degradation reduced. Pager cleared for now but monitor for 2h.

-- end of thread --
